title: Foundations of Quantum Mechanics
scope: The operator formalism of quantum mechanics: the postulates and Dirac notation, measurement and collapse, expectation values and uncertainty, compatible and incompatible operators (with the uncertainty relation), the Dirac delta function and the position and momentum representations, time evolution (the time-evolution operator, stationary states, the Schr\"odinger and Heisenberg pictures), the one-dimensional time-independent Schr\"odinger equation, the linear harmonic oscillator by the ladder-operator method, and coherent states.

chapters.title: Postulates of Quantum Mechanics and Dirac Notation
Compatible and Incompatible Operators
Dirac Delta Function and the Position and Momentum Bases
Time Evolution: Stationary States and the Schrödinger and Heisenberg Pictures
The One-Dimensional Time-Independent Schrödinger Equation
The Linear Harmonic Oscillator: Ladder-Operator Method
Classical Limit of the Oscillator: Coherent States

title: Symmetry, Angular Momentum and Clebsch-Gordan Coefficients
scope: This part covers symmetry and conservation laws in quantum mechanics: translation and time translation (momentum and energy conservation, the time-evolution operator), rotations and the angular momentum algebra, spin-$\tfrac12$ and the Pauli matrices, the $j=1$ representation, rotation matrices, orbital angular momentum and spherical harmonics, addition of angular momenta with Clebsch-Gordan coefficients, spin-orbit coupling (the sodium doublet, the Zeeman and Paschen-Back limits) and central potentials.

chapters.title: Translation Symmetry and Conservation of Momentum
Time Translation and the Time-Evolution Operator
Rotations, Isotropy of Space and Angular Momentum Conservation
Angular Momentum: Eigenvalues and Ladder Operators
Spin-1/2 and the Pauli Matrices
The j=1 Representation and the Angular Momentum Uncertainty Relation
Rotation Matrices (Wigner D-Matrices)
Orbital Angular Momentum and Spherical Harmonics
Addition of Angular Momenta
Clebsch-Gordan Tables
Spin-Orbit Coupling: the Doublet in Sodium
Central Potentials

title: Tensor Operators, Wigner-Eckart and the Projection Theorem
scope: This part covers how operators transform under rotations: scalar and vector operators, Cartesian tensors and their decomposition into irreducible pieces, irreducible spherical tensor operators and their commutation relations with $\hat{\vec J}$, the Wigner-Eckart theorem (with the dipole matrix element and the selection rules as the main application), and the projection theorem (with the spin expectation value and the Land\'e factor as applications). It continues directly from Part~II on angular momentum and Clebsch-Gordan coefficients.

chapters.title: Scalar and Vector Operators
Cartesian Tensors: Reducible and Irreducible
Irreducible Tensor Operators and Their Commutation Relations
The Wigner-Eckart Theorem
Application: Dipole Matrix Elements and Selection Rules
The Projection Theorem

title: Time-Independent Approximation Methods
scope: Time-independent perturbation theory (non-degenerate and degenerate, with the hydrogen fine structure and Zeeman applications), the variational method, and the WKB approximation.

chapters.title: Time-Independent Perturbation Theory: Non-Degenerate Case
Time-Independent Perturbation Theory: Degenerate Case
Applications to Hydrogen: Fine Structure and the Zeeman Effect
The Variational Method
The WKB Approximation

title: Time-Dependent Perturbation Theory
scope: Time-dependent perturbation theory: the two-level system, the interaction picture and the Dyson series, Rabi oscillations, first and second order transition amplitudes, harmonic perturbations and Fermi's golden rule, the adiabatic and sudden approximations, emission and absorption of radiation (Einstein coefficients, spontaneous emission, selection rules), and time translation with conservation of energy.
